# R370 — decode route reuse instrumentation, source-only design review

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Target worktree: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013`. Read-only review; this report is the only file created. No build, test, model/GPU run, profiler, service action, code change, or Git operation was performed. Main owns the concurrent source/build work. This is an implementation proposal, not measured cache benefit.

## Source identity and concurrent edits

The target worktree's commit identity at inspection was `410904c99d273435b5302fa8976cc667d17957f2`, the same commit as the fixed-source comparison worktree `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/diag-native-copy-queue-qualified-20261013`. Fixed-source path was explicitly pinned by the task to commit `410904c99d273435b5302fa8976cc667d17957f2`; no performance measurement was made against either tree. Lines below refer to the fixed-source tree at that commit; dirty target changes can shift line numbers and must be reconciled before implementation.

Read the R364–R369 reports in `research-20261009`, including R369 v1 and its arithmetic correction v2. The registered history pointer supplied by Main is EXACT `report-registry-v185.json`, `research_completed=894`. R364–R369 addressed full-context admission, scratch-alias route review, head/phase-cache leases, prefill admission, and corrected decode packed-set arithmetic. R369 v2 is authoritative for arithmetic: one expert across 48 layers is 98,227,200 B; top-10 across 48 layers is 982,272,000 B (936.77 MiB); 512 experts sum to 50,292,326,400 B. Window union bounds W=2/4/8 are limits, not observed locality. This report adds the missing source ownership/timing gate and an exact low-cost observer contract; it does not repeat a claim that “aggregate routes” alone establishes benefit.

## Finding: where IDs exist, and when the host may read them

The router outputs are initially device-side. `src/core/layer.cpp:360-390` computes logits and topK, then `doorbell_publish` copies activation, IDs, and weights to the host handoff and rings last. On the Xe path, `src/kernels/xe/router.cpp:55-145,147-162,169-231` submits topK asynchronously when given a stream; it does not make those device result buffers host-readable. A CPU observer must consume the host-owned route copy after a real producer-completion boundary.

The safest existing seam for ordinary one-token decode is `src/core/session.cpp:696-724`, inside `session_loop`: graph work is followed by `event_sync(probe)` (lines 699-706), which is a normal SYCL event wait, then `pool(...)` receives `s.db->h_ids`/`h_weights` at line 723. The event covers producer graph work and the handoff writes. The callback's route IDs remain valid for the duration of that call; the same fixed handoff buffer is rewritten by later graph submissions, so an observer must copy IDs into its own small ring synchronously before returning. It must not retain the pointer. This adds no event, stream wait, host-USM polling, or device command. With `pool == nullptr` (GPU-only path) there is no callback, so this signal is absent by construction.

The synchronous `drive_pool` wrapper at `src/program/generate.cpp:804-832` is reached from this seam. Its layer identity must be captured carefully: `expert_pool_dispatch` advances `d.layers`; the callback currently derives the consumed layer as `d.layers - 1` after dispatch (lines 817-821). An observer placed in the wrapper should capture that layer before dispatch or use the same validated post-dispatch value. It must not consult `d.layers` asynchronously. `drive_pool_multi` at lines 834-854 receives the layer explicitly, but it is called by several Verifier paths.

Important exception: `session_run_token` at `src/core/session.cpp:923-980` uses a `TokenGraph` and spins on a mapped host sequence at lines 937-959, then calls the pool at 971. Its comments/guard require `host_handoff_concurrent`; task-supplied capability evidence says shared host USM and host-USM concurrent atomics are unsupported on the current B570 (`ATOMIC_HOST_USM=0`). Do not infer that the volatile sequence loop makes route payload access safe, and do not add more host polling. The regular `session_loop` is the candidate route for instrumentation, subject to its existing event-based ownership boundary.

Verify/pipelined issuance is not currently a safe CPU read seam under the task's constraint. `Verifier::run`/`batch_poll`/`service` observe `h_seq_` and then pass `h_ids_` to `drive_pool_multi` (`src/core/verify.cpp:1497-1578`, `2035-2085`, `2192-2235`, `2552-2612`). `batch_poll` is invoked by `StagePoll` threads when `--batch-cpu-split` is active (`src/program/generate.cpp:7592-7638`); those callbacks may run concurrently on separate `Drive` objects. The current sequence is a device-written host-USM signal polled before producer completion, not a SYCL event completion. `std::atomic_thread_fence`, `_mm_sfence`, and `volatile` after the callback do not establish a valid CPU/GPU concurrent shared-memory handoff for the route payload. A callback-local CPU-only aggregate merged with atomics would solve CPU-vs-CPU races but cannot legalize the GPU-vs-CPU route read. Therefore exclude verify/pipelined requests from v1 route telemetry unless Main first supplies an already-required, supported per-window completion event before the callback. Adding such a wait solely for telemetry fails the no-added-sync requirement. Do not silently aggregate these paths as if their source contract matched `session_loop`.

CPU router/fallback: when topK itself is computed on CPU, IDs are ordinary CPU-owned data and can be observed at the same synchronous dispatch boundary with no device race. In this target the standard Xe router is a SYCL kernel, so this is a fallback/property of a true CPU-routing implementation, not a general license to read GPU output. Any fallback must report its path separately; do not combine fallback routes into a GPU decode result without labeling.

## Minimal observer contract and exact insertion point

Recommendation: add an opt-in, request-scoped `RouteReuseObserver` owned by `Drive`, enabled only for the safe `session_loop`/single-token route. Keep it out of `ExpertDispatch` and worker jobs. At `drive_pool` entry, copy the 10 IDs to a stack-local `std::array<int32_t,10>` after validating `k` and ranges; at callback return update the observer using the captured layer. The easiest no-allocation hot-path contract is a fixed-size member ring and counters allocated before generation. It stores no token IDs beyond the last eight route sets, writes no per-token/per-layer records, and emits only final numeric aggregates. The owner thread is the synchronous callback thread; if routes from multiple independent CPU callbacks are ever admitted, each callback must accumulate into local fixed storage and merge via CPU-only atomics or a lock after dispatch, never let worker threads mutate the ring. For this initial no-pipeline scope, a simple single-owner observer avoids atomics entirely.

State, allocated once per request/reset:

* `[48][8][10]` small route IDs with valid-count/sequence tags (15,360 bytes if int32), plus 48 per-layer 512-bit membership scratch (3,072 bytes) for each newly completed window. `k=10`, `n_expert=512`, and layer count should be checked against the model geometry rather than assumed for a generalized engine.
* For each W in `{2,4,8}`, maintain per-layer per-expert reference counts over the active W slots (48×512 counters; uint8 suffices for W≤8) and exact unique count; on eviction decrement each ID, on insert increment. Sum `unique_count[layer] * blob_bytes(layer)` for packed-byte union. Report the total distribution (min/median/p95/max by completed sliding window) and per-token amortized sum. Warm-up windows of fewer than W routes are excluded from full-W summaries and counted separately. These are sliding consecutive decode windows, not disjoint groups.
* Maintain independent exact per-layer LRU state for capacities 3 and 19: fixed `[48][19]` IDs, valid length, and an LRU order. For each observed ID, count request/hit/miss and add `blob_bytes(layer)` to weighted hit/miss bytes. Count repeated IDs in a single route only once for cache recency/statistics (IDs are expected distinct topK, but validate this invariant). Reset empty at request start and state the cold-start policy. For C=3, LRU3's 3-entry list is independently simulated; it is not the first three entries of LRU19.
* Compare each route against the loaded static profile's first 19 per-layer pairs, as present in the `profile` vector read by `read_expert_profile` (`src/program/generate.cpp:2316,3032+`) and consumed for cache admission around lines 3150-3190 / `host_res` initialization. Count static-top19 request IDs and byte-weighted hits. If no valid profile is loaded, report `static_top19=unavailable`; do not substitute observed-run frequency as the static policy. The profile rank may contain fewer than 19 pairs in a layer; use actual available rank count and report it.
* Also record routed entry count, distinct IDs/window, route callback count, per-layer route count, observed path/mode, invalid-ID count, and whether GPU-resident hits were visible. If actual `host_res` membership is accessible without a separate load or race, separately count GPU-cache hits at dispatch entry; otherwise label this “route-only modeled.” Do not infer cache-source traffic from the ID trace.

The model is top10 across 48 layers. The corrected R369 v2 byte table and arithmetic may be reused; blob byte weight is constant by layer, so an exact distinct-ID count per layer multiplied by that layer's `blob_bytes` is sufficient. No raw route IDs need to be persisted. Log only request summary values, profile identity/hash, reset scope, and validation counters. Do not dump token text, logs, inputs, or routing traces. Keep aggregate values in the normal request result or one short diagnostic record; persistent full history is unnecessary for this question.

The callback already accounts dispatch time using `Clock::now()` in `generate.cpp:808-811`; telemetry should avoid a second clock/timer on every token if no timing split is needed. For instrumentation overhead validation, use a correctness-only synthetic observer fixture (no model/GPU) only if Main requests it; this assignment ran no tests. Add no SYCL kernel, USM allocation, copy, queue, event, or profiling tag. Because the counter update itself is CPU work on the decode thread, the final acceptance criterion is that the opt-in aggregate's observed callback CPU overhead is negligible and the stock benchmark's decode distribution does not regress; do not use custom GEN performance as a substitute.

## How to interpret the four comparisons

1. **Sliding W=2/4/8 unions** estimate repeated packed-set identities across adjacent token routes. Report exact min/median/p95/max and amortized unique bytes per token. This measures logical distinct source extents only. It does not measure DRAM lines/transactions, LLC, OS page-cache hits, actual read calls, DMA, CPU decode time saved, or end-to-end speed.
2. **Static top-19** answers whether the current profile's exact per-layer ranked set covers route entries, weighted by blob bytes. It has zero temporal adaptation in this simulation. It does not establish that the current VRAM cache admitted/kept those rows, that cache hits save the full blob read, or that profile identity matches the request domain.
3. **LRU3 and LRU19** answer whether an ideal per-layer bounded identity cache, starting cold, would retain byte-weighted route working sets under this request. These are counterfactual host/source-reuse curves. They do not include cache fill latency, eviction write/copy, GPU synchronization, capacity contention, coalesced reads, future concurrency, request-to-request carryover, or actual page-cache reuse. Report entry hit rate and byte hit rate separately; do not call either physical memory traffic.
4. **Actual output correctness and serving rate** remain independent gates. The latest task-supplied stock result is upstream `bench.sh --long --runs3`, input 32,049 with all input read/reuse 0/output 24; COPY0 prefill/decode medians 407.5/8.6 and COPY1 474.8/8.7. Decode ranges overlap and sustained 70 tok/s was not met. These prior numbers motivate a decode-only diagnostic but do not validate this observer or prove caching would help.

No rate ceiling may be inferred from `982,272,000 B/token`, set unions, or byte-hit estimates. Logical unique blob extents do not equal physical RAM transactions; actual reused source pages can remain in LLC or OS page cache, while a logical cache hit can still incur bookkeeping/fill costs.

## Adoption gate and recommended order

**Accept as a bounded diagnostic** only if all conditions hold: (a) instrumentation is opt-in and restricted to one GPU/no-MTP, single-token `session_loop` decode; (b) callback is demonstrably after the existing successful `event_sync(probe)` and before its host route buffer can be overwritten; (c) no additional synchronization, polling, event, queue operation, raw route persistence, or model output change is introduced; (d) request reset boundaries are explicit and concurrent worker callbacks cannot write shared non-atomic state; (e) profile top19 is labeled by exact profile identity, or unavailable; (f) counters match a deterministic CPU-only route fixture including duplicates, invalid IDs, cold start, and W warm-up; (g) stock upstream benchmark confirms no meaningful decode regression and outputs pass the existing correctness gate.

**Reject/defer** if it requires reading mapped host-USM while the device may write it, shared or host-USM concurrent atomics, a new queue wait, an extra D2H copy, route trace dumping, or merging verify/pipelined callbacks without a pre-existing completion event. Defer dynamic LRU implementation if the diagnostic shows no material route-only byte-hit opportunity beyond static top19, or if only request-global rather than within-decode recurrence exists. Consider actual cache work only after a held-out workload demonstrates stable byte-weighted reuse and subsequent stock paired measurements show correct outputs plus improvement in decode wall distribution; use source/cache hit telemetry and CPU expert service time to test the mechanism, not logical bytes as a proxy.

Recommended priority:

1. **Proceed with CPU-only observer design review** for the event-completed single-token callback. No model measurement is needed to settle ownership and reset logic.
2. **Defer runtime instrumentation merge into active phase-cache edits** until Main's current source/build inspection closes; this report observed dirty concurrent source.
3. **Exclude verify, batch, MTP and pipelined issuer from the first diagnostic.** If later required, first establish a standards-supported ownership transfer/completion contract under the B570 capability limits, separately from the cache experiment.
4. **Decide cache policy only from measured aggregates and later stock A/B**, with the counterfactual nature clearly disclosed.

## External implementation evidence

These sources support dataflow/design comparisons, not transfer of their performance numbers to Strata's Xe/B570 path:

* vLLM's real [routed-experts capturer source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts_capturer.py) captures topK IDs, copies worker capture data to scheduler output, then stores arrays in CPU-owned slot-indexed memory; it documents that NumPy fancy-index returns a copy safe across later writes. It is explicit evidence that capture needs a well-defined ownership/retention boundary and that storing full histories can consume substantial memory. It is a CUDA/PyTorch scheduler feature, not a zero-sync Strata recipe.
* vLLM's [EPLB deployment docs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md) say routing statistics are collected on each forward and periodically used to rebalance placement. That is load balancing, not evidence of temporal reuse or a local per-token cache speedup.
* SGLang's [expert parallelism documentation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/advanced_features/expert_parallelism.mdx) describes TopK output flowing into dispatch and its EPLB's expert activation statistics. It corroborates the practical route/dispatch seam, but its scale-out, batch and dispatcher architecture does not establish safe host observation for this single-GPU SYCL engine.
* Intel's [llm-scaler repository](https://github.com/intel/llm-scaler) identifies a vLLM-based Intel serving stack and MoE support. The inspected search results did not expose an authoritative source showing a local time-direction expert cache at the relevant seam; do not cite it as proof of this design or its gains.
* A directly relevant independent implementation is [ap03906101/moe-hotcache](https://github.com/ap03906101/moe-hotcache), which describes runtime hot-expert caching in llama.cpp, an adjacent-token overlap statistic, and explicit quarantine of an evicted slot for one cycle so an in-flight graph cannot read overwritten storage. It is self-reported implementation evidence, not an independently validated performance result. Its slot-lifetime point reinforces that any eventual Strata residency mutation needs an execution-use retirement boundary.
* A personal [Mini-SGLang MoE write-up](https://nothiny.github.io/2026/09/15/mini-moe/) compares LRU, LFU, frequency-decay and LRU-K under a small cache and describes LRU thrash under gradual routing drift. This is a blog/implementation report; it justifies testing more than a static popularity rank but does not establish an optimal policy for Strata.
* vLLM's [MoE offload RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38256) includes a concrete warning from an implementer: prefill frequency can go stale after the generation topic changes; it also distinguishes policy hit rates from actual decode benefit. This supports request-local reset and held-out/static-vs-LRU comparisons, while being RFC discussion rather than merged design evidence.

The concurrency and memory-ownership conclusion is instead grounded in the primary [SYCL 2020 specification](https://registry.khronos.org/SYCL/specs/sycl-2020/html/sycl-2020.html?from=20423&from_column=20423), whose event semantics allow host code to wait for represented actions to complete, and its [host/device interaction reference](https://github.khronos.org/SYCL_Reference/iface/interaction-with-host-code.html), which describes concurrent host/device USM access/atomics as capability-dependent. The [USM reference](https://github.khronos.org/SYCL_Reference/iface/usm_allocations.html) demonstrates queue completion before the host reads a result. This matches the source's explicit `event_sync(probe)` ownership boundary and the supplied `ATOMIC_HOST_USM=0` exclusion; a CPU memory fence alone is not a device completion event.

## Final decision

The low-risk useful first step is a bounded, request-scoped, CPU-only aggregate at the `drive_pool` callback used by event-completed `session_loop`, collecting exact W=2/4/8 sliding union bytes, static profile top19 byte coverage, and independent cold LRU3/LRU19 byte hit ratios. Do not include verify/pipelined issuers until they expose a pre-existing supported completion boundary. Keep only aggregate counters and hashes; no raw IDs or trace files. Treat all modeled bytes as logical extents and require a later stock paired run before any performance claim.
